```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Function for getting sample lists from tables quickly using existing index
get_pg_table_samples <- function(db, table, sampleid_col){
  # Makes use of the SQL index, *much* faster to run
  query <- sql(str_glue("WITH RECURSIVE t AS (
     SELECT min(\"{sampleid_col}\") AS sample FROM \"{table}\"
     UNION ALL
     SELECT (SELECT min(\"{sampleid_col}\") FROM \"{table}\" WHERE \"{sampleid_col}\" > t.sample)
     FROM t WHERE t.sample IS NOT NULL
     )
  SELECT sample FROM t WHERE sample IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT null WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM \"{table}\" WHERE \"{sampleid_col}\" IS NULL);"))
  
  mapped_samples <- DBI::dbGetQuery(db, query)
  return(mapped_samples)
}
```

# Create bin summary view table
```{r}
checkm_pg <- tbl(pg, "checkm")
gtdb_pg <- tbl(pg, "GTDB")
drep_pg <- tbl(pg, "drep")
sampinfo_pg <- tbl(pg, "glamr_samples")


bin_info_view <- checkm_pg %>% 
  select(sample, bin, Completeness, Contamination, `Strain heterogeneity`) %>% 
  #mutate(SampleID = str_remove(bin, "[A-z].*_d\\+$")) %>% 
  left_join(sampinfo_pg %>% select(sample = "SampleID", StudyID)) %>% 
  left_join(gtdb_pg %>% select(sample, bin, classification, domain, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species, red_value)) %>% 
  left_join(drep_pg %>% select(sample, bin, secondary_cluster, drep_score, is_cluster_rep)) %>% 
  show_query()

sql_query <- glue::glue_sql("
CREATE VIEW bin_summary AS
WITH extracted AS (
  SELECT
    \"bin\",
    \"Completeness\",
    \"Contamination\",
    \"Strain heterogeneity\",
    (regexp_matches(\"bin\", '^(.+_\\d+)_(.+?)_(\\d+)$'))[1] AS \"sample\",
    (regexp_matches(\"bin\", '^(.+_\\d+)_(.+?)_(\\d+)$'))[2] AS \"binner\",
    (regexp_matches(\"bin\", '^(.+_\\d+)_(.+?)_(\\d+)$'))[3] AS \"bin_number\"
  FROM \"checkm\")
SELECT
  extracted.\"bin\",
  extracted.\"sample\",
  \"glamr_samples\".\"StudyID\",
  extracted.\"binner\",
  extracted.\"bin_number\",
  extracted.\"Completeness\",
  extracted.\"Contamination\",
  extracted.\"Strain heterogeneity\",
  \"GTDB\".\"classification\",
  \"GTDB\".\"domain\",
  \"GTDB\".\"phylum\",
  \"GTDB\".\"class\",
  \"GTDB\".\"order\",
  \"GTDB\".\"family\",
  \"GTDB\".\"genus\",
  \"GTDB\".\"species\",
  \"GTDB\".\"red_value\",
  \"drep\".\"secondary_cluster\",
  \"drep\".\"drep_score\",
  \"drep\".\"is_cluster_rep\"
FROM extracted
LEFT JOIN \"glamr_samples\"
  ON extracted.\"sample\" = \"glamr_samples\".\"SampleID\"
LEFT JOIN \"GTDB\"
  ON extracted.\"bin\" = \"GTDB\".\"bin\"
LEFT JOIN \"drep\"
  ON extracted.\"bin\" = \"drep\".\"bin\";", .con = pg)

DBI::dbSendQuery(pg, sql_query)
```


#### Load taxonomic information
Output of: 
  taxonkit list --ids 1 -n > references/taxonkit/taxon_names.txt
  taxonkit list --ids 1 | taxonkit lineage | taxonkit reformat -a -i 2 -P > references/taxonkit/standardized_lineages.txt


```{r}
tax_cols <- c("tax_id", "full_lineage", "rank", "std_lineage")
taxa_list_std <- read_tsv("~/references/taxonkit/standardized_lineages_with_rank.txt",col_names = tax_cols)

tax_info <- taxa_list_std %>% 
  separate(std_lineage, into = c("kingdom", "phylum", "class", "order", "family", "genus", "species"),sep = ";[a-z]__" ,remove = FALSE) %>% 
  mutate(tax_name = str_remove(full_lineage, ".*;"),
         kingdom = str_remove(kingdom, "^k__")) %>% 
  relocate(tax_id, tax_name, rank, full_lineage, std_lineage)

dbWriteTable(pg,"tax_info", tax_info, overwrite = TRUE)
sql('CREATE INDEX "tax_info_tax_id" ON "tax_info" ("tax_id")') %>% DBI::dbSendQuery(pg, .)
sql('CREATE INDEX "tax_info_tax_name" ON "tax_info" ("tax_name")') %>% DBI::dbSendQuery(pg, .)
sql('CREATE INDEX "tax_info_rank" ON "tax_info" ("rank")') %>% DBI::dbSendQuery(pg, .)
```

```{r}
# Get read counts already loaded into the database
existing_read_counts <- tbl(pg, "read_count") %>% collect()

existing_read_count_samples <- get_pg_table_samples(pg, "read_count", "sample")

# Find read count tsvs
read_count_paths <- Sys.glob("data/omics/*/*/reads/*_read_count_fastp.tsv") %>% 
  data.frame(path = .) %>% 
  bind_cols(.,unglue::unglue_data(.$path,"data/omics/{sample_type}/{sample}/reads/{sample2}_read_count_fastp.tsv")) %>% 
  bind_cols(file.info(.$path))

# Filter read count tsvs to only those not already loaded in the database
new_read_count_paths <- read_count_paths %>% 
  filter(!sample %in% existing_read_count_samples$sample,
         sample == sample2)
```

```{r}
# Function to read count tsv and load into the database
read_tsv_to_pg <- function(path, sample) {
  states <- c("raw_reads", "deduped_reads", "filt_and_trimmed_reads", "decon_reads")

  print(sample)

  # Only used when creating the table for the first time, for all subsequent additions, append = TRUE should be added and the field types are already established
  postgres_col_types = c(read_state = 'text',
                         direction = 'text',
                         count = 'bigint',
                         sample = 'text',
                         percent_retained = 'numeric',
                         percent_removed = 'numeric',
                         method = 'text')
  
  
  tryCatch({
    read_tsv(path, col_types = "cnn") %>%
      pivot_longer(-read_state, names_to = "direction", values_to = "count") %>%
      mutate(sample = sample,
             direction = str_remove(direction, "_read_count"),
             read_state = factor(read_state, levels = states, ordered = TRUE)) %>%
      arrange(sample, direction, read_state) %>%
      group_by(sample, direction) %>%
      mutate(
        percent_retained = count / lag(count) * 100,
        percent_removed = (lag(count) - count) / lag(count) * 100,
        method = "Fastp"
      ) %>%
      dbWriteTable(pg, "read_count", ., overwrite = FALSE,
                   append = TRUE # Has to be false if table doesn't exit yet
                   #,field.types = postgres_col_types
                   )
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("Error occurred while processing file:", path, "\n")
    cat("Error message:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
  })
}

walk2(new_read_count_paths$path, new_read_count_paths$sample, read_tsv_to_pg)
```

## Read stats (seqkit)
```{r}
# Rule seqkit_stats writes `seqkit stats --all --tabular` for each read file to
# data/omics/{sample_type}/{sample}/reads/read_stats/{reads}.txt. Intended to replace the
# read_count table above (count_reads_fastp) as the primary source of read stats.
read_stats_table <- "read_stats"

# Optionally limit loading to specific studies, NULL loads every sample with read stats
read_stats_studies <- NULL # e.g. c("set_132", "set_127")

# Dedup key is (sample, reads), not just sample: read stats files for a sample are produced
# by separate jobs (and metaT samples get extra read states), so they can arrive over several runs
if (DBI::dbExistsTable(pg, read_stats_table)) {
  existing_read_stats <- tbl(pg, read_stats_table) %>%
    select(sample, reads) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    collect()
} else {
  existing_read_stats <- tibble(sample = character(), reads = character())
}

# Find all seqkit stats files
read_stats_paths <- Sys.glob("data/omics/*/*/reads/read_stats/*.txt") %>%
  data.frame(path = .) %>%
  bind_cols(., unglue::unglue_data(.$path, "data/omics/{sample_type}/{sample}/reads/read_stats/{reads}.txt"))

if (!is.null(read_stats_studies)) {
  read_stats_study_samples <- tbl(pg, "glamr_samples") %>%
    filter(StudyID %in% read_stats_studies) %>%
    pull(SampleID)

  read_stats_paths <- read_stats_paths %>%
    filter(sample %in% read_stats_study_samples)
}

# Filter to only those not already loaded into the database
new_read_stats <- read_stats_paths %>%
  anti_join(existing_read_stats, by = c("sample", "reads")) %>%
  filter(str_detect(sample, "^samp_") | str_detect(sample, "^coassembly_") | str_detect(sample, "^GVHDsamp_"))

# Initialize the mirai cluster for parallel tsv parsing prior to upload
n_cores <- parallel::detectCores() - 1
daemons(n_cores)

message(paste("Processing", nrow(new_read_stats), "seqkit stats files across", n_cores, "cores..."))

everywhere({
  library(dplyr)
  library(readr)
  library(stringr)
  library(janitor)
})

# Explicit column types so files with zero reads (empty min/avg/max etc.) don't get guessed
# as logical and clash with the others when binding. clean_names() turns e.g. "Q20(%)" into
# q20_percent and "GC(%)" into gc_percent.
read_seqkit_stats_parallel <- function(path, sample_type, sample, reads) {
  tryCatch({
    read_tsv(path, show_col_types = FALSE,
             col_types = cols(file = "c", format = "c", type = "c", .default = "d")) %>%
      janitor::clean_names() %>%
      select(-file) %>%
      mutate(sample_type = sample_type,
             sample = sample,
             reads = reads,
             # e.g. decon_fwd_reads_fastp -> direction "fwd", read_state "decon_reads_fastp"
             direction = str_extract(reads, "(?<=_)(fwd|rev)(?=_)"),
             read_state = str_remove(reads, "_(fwd|rev)(?=_)"),
             mod_time = file.info(path)$mtime) %>%
      relocate(sample_type, sample, reads, read_state, direction)
  }, error = function(e) return(conditionMessage(e)))
}

combined_read_stats_results <- mirai_map(
  .x = new_read_stats %>% select(path, sample_type, sample, reads),
  .f = read_seqkit_stats_parallel
)

# This waits for all workers to finish
read_stats_results_list <- combined_read_stats_results[]

# read_seqkit_stats_parallel returns the error message instead of a data frame when a file fails to parse
failed_read_stats <- read_stats_results_list %>% discard(is.data.frame)
if (length(failed_read_stats) > 0) {
  warning(length(failed_read_stats), " seqkit stats files failed to parse and were skipped:\n",
          paste(new_read_stats$path[!map_lgl(read_stats_results_list, is.data.frame)], unlist(failed_read_stats), sep = ": ", collapse = "\n"))
}

combined_read_stats_data <- read_stats_results_list %>%
  keep(is.data.frame) %>%
  list_rbind()

daemons(0)

if (nrow(combined_read_stats_data) > 0) {
  message("Uploading to Postgres...")

  dbExecute(pg, 'DROP INDEX IF EXISTS public.read_stats_sample')
  dbExecute(pg, 'DROP INDEX IF EXISTS public.read_stats_reads')

  dbWriteTable(pg, read_stats_table, combined_read_stats_data, append = TRUE, row.names = FALSE)

  dbExecute(pg, str_glue('CREATE INDEX "read_stats_sample" ON "{read_stats_table}" ("sample")'))
  dbExecute(pg, str_glue('CREATE INDEX "read_stats_reads" ON "{read_stats_table}" ("reads")'))

  message("Success!")
}
```

## Sylph
Rules sylph, sylph_ribodeplete, and sylph_hifi each write a genome-level `sylph profile` tsv
({read_set}profile-{database}.tsv) plus a clade-level `sylph-tax taxprof` file named after the
read file ({read_file}.fastq.gz.sylphmpa). The two tables can be joined on (sample, read_file).

##### Genome profiles
```{r}
sylph_profile_table <- "sylph_profile"

# Optionally limit loading to specific studies, NULL loads every sample with sylph results
sylph_studies <- NULL # e.g. c("set_115")

# Dedup key is (sample, read_set, database): metaT samples get both standard and ribodepleted
# profiles, and profiles against new databases can be added later
if (DBI::dbExistsTable(pg, sylph_profile_table)) {
  existing_sylph_profiles <- tbl(pg, sylph_profile_table) %>%
    select(sample, read_set, database) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    collect()
} else {
  existing_sylph_profiles <- tibble(sample = character(), read_set = character(), database = character())
}

# Find all sylph profiles, read_set is the profile name prefix ("" for the standard rule)
sylph_profile_paths <- Sys.glob("data/omics/*/*/sylph/*profile-*.tsv") %>%
  data.frame(path = .) %>%
  bind_cols(., unglue::unglue_data(.$path, "data/omics/{sample_type}/{sample}/sylph/{profile_file}.tsv")) %>%
  mutate(read_set = str_remove(profile_file, "_?profile-.*") %>% na_if("") %>% replace_na("standard"),
         database = str_remove(profile_file, ".*profile-"))

if (!is.null(sylph_studies)) {
  sylph_study_samples <- tbl(pg, "glamr_samples") %>%
    filter(StudyID %in% sylph_studies) %>%
    pull(SampleID)

  sylph_profile_paths <- sylph_profile_paths %>%
    filter(sample %in% sylph_study_samples)
}

# Filter to only those not already loaded into the database
new_sylph_profiles <- sylph_profile_paths %>%
  anti_join(existing_sylph_profiles, by = c("sample", "read_set", "database")) %>%
  filter(str_detect(sample, "^samp_") | str_detect(sample, "^coassembly_") | str_detect(sample, "^GVHDsamp_"))

# Initialize the mirai cluster for parallel tsv parsing prior to upload
n_cores <- parallel::detectCores() - 1
daemons(n_cores)

message(paste("Processing", nrow(new_sylph_profiles), "sylph profiles across", n_cores, "cores..."))

everywhere({
  library(dplyr)
  library(readr)
  library(stringr)
  library(janitor)
})

# Explicit column types: Eff_lambda is "HIGH" or a number, and the percentile/containment
# columns are ranges/ratios (e.g. "NA-NA", "17821/19424"), so those are kept as text
read_sylph_profile_parallel <- function(path, sample_type, sample, read_set, database) {
  tryCatch({
    read_tsv(path, show_col_types = FALSE,
             col_types = cols(Sample_file = "c", Genome_file = "c", `ANI_5-95_percentile` = "c",
                              Eff_lambda = "c", `Lambda_5-95_percentile` = "c", Containment_ind = "c",
                              Contig_name = "c", .default = "d")) %>%
      janitor::clean_names() %>%
      # Older sylph versions (e.g. samp_447's early test run) called true_cov eff_cov
      dplyr::rename(any_of(c(true_cov = "eff_cov"))) %>%
      mutate(sample_type = sample_type,
             sample = sample,
             read_set = read_set,
             database = database,
             read_file = basename(sample_file) %>% str_remove("\\.f(ast)?q\\.gz$"),
             # Matches the t__ strain accession in the sylph-tax output
             genome = basename(genome_file) %>% str_remove("_genomic\\.fna\\.gz$")) %>%
      select(-sample_file) %>%
      relocate(sample_type, sample, read_set, database, read_file, genome)
  }, error = function(e) return(conditionMessage(e)))
}

combined_sylph_profile_results <- mirai_map(
  .x = new_sylph_profiles %>% select(path, sample_type, sample, read_set, database),
  .f = read_sylph_profile_parallel
)

sylph_profile_results_list <- combined_sylph_profile_results[]

# read_sylph_profile_parallel returns the error message instead of a data frame when a file fails to parse
failed_sylph_profiles <- sylph_profile_results_list %>% discard(is.data.frame)
if (length(failed_sylph_profiles) > 0) {
  warning(length(failed_sylph_profiles), " sylph profiles failed to parse and were skipped:\n",
          paste(new_sylph_profiles$path[!map_lgl(sylph_profile_results_list, is.data.frame)], unlist(failed_sylph_profiles), sep = ": ", collapse = "\n"))
}

combined_sylph_profile_data <- sylph_profile_results_list %>%
  keep(is.data.frame) %>%
  list_rbind()

daemons(0)

if (nrow(combined_sylph_profile_data) > 0) {
  message("Uploading to Postgres...")

  dbExecute(pg, 'DROP INDEX IF EXISTS public.sylph_profile_sample')
  dbExecute(pg, 'DROP INDEX IF EXISTS public.sylph_profile_genome')

  dbWriteTable(pg, sylph_profile_table, combined_sylph_profile_data, append = TRUE, row.names = FALSE)

  dbExecute(pg, str_glue('CREATE INDEX "sylph_profile_sample" ON "{sylph_profile_table}" ("sample")'))
  dbExecute(pg, str_glue('CREATE INDEX "sylph_profile_genome" ON "{sylph_profile_table}" ("genome")'))

  message("Success!")
}
```

```{r}
# Initialize the mirai cluster for parallel tsv parsing prior to upload
n_cores <- parallel::detectCores() - 1
daemons(n_cores)

message(paste("Processing", nrow(new_sylph_taxprofs), "sylph-tax profiles across", n_cores, "cores..."))

everywhere({
  library(dplyr)
  library(readr)
  library(stringr)
  library(tidyr)
})

# The first line is a "#SampleID ... Taxonomies_used:['GTDB_r232']" comment, the header is on line 2.
# Each row is one clade (domain down to t__ strain/genome), with the lineage split into rank columns
# so e.g. genus-level rows are simply rank == "genus".
read_sylph_taxprof_parallel <- function(path, sample_type, sample, read_file) {
  tryCatch({
    taxonomy <- read_lines(path, n_max = 1) %>% str_extract("(?<=Taxonomies_used:\\[').*(?='\\])")

    read_tsv(path, skip = 1, show_col_types = FALSE,
             col_types = cols(clade_name = "c", .default = "d")) %>%
      dplyr::rename(ani = "ANI (if strain-level)", coverage = "Coverage (if strain-level)") %>%
      mutate(rank = str_extract(clade_name, "[a-z](?=__[^|]*$)") %>%
               recode(d = "domain", p = "phylum", c = "class", o = "order", f = "family", g = "genus", s = "species", t = "genome"),
             taxon = str_remove(clade_name, ".*\\|") %>% str_remove("^[a-z]__")) %>%
      separate_wider_delim(clade_name, delim = "|", names = c("domain", "phylum", "class", "order", "family", "genus", "species", "genome"),
                           too_few = "align_start", cols_remove = FALSE) %>%
      mutate(across(domain:genome, ~ str_remove(.x, "^[a-z]__")),
             sample_type = sample_type,
             sample = sample,
             read_file = read_file,
             taxonomy = taxonomy) %>%
      relocate(sample_type, sample, read_file, taxonomy, rank, taxon, clade_name)
  }, error = function(e) return(conditionMessage(e)))
}

combined_sylph_taxprof_results <- mirai_map(
  .x = new_sylph_taxprofs %>% select(path, sample_type, sample, read_file),
  .f = read_sylph_taxprof_parallel
)

sylph_taxprof_results_list <- combined_sylph_taxprof_results[]

# read_sylph_taxprof_parallel returns the error message instead of a data frame when a file fails to parse
failed_sylph_taxprofs <- sylph_taxprof_results_list %>% discard(is.data.frame)
if (length(failed_sylph_taxprofs) > 0) {
  warning(length(failed_sylph_taxprofs), " sylph-tax profiles failed to parse and were skipped:\n",
          paste(new_sylph_taxprofs$path[!map_lgl(sylph_taxprof_results_list, is.data.frame)], unlist(failed_sylph_taxprofs), sep = ": ", collapse = "\n"))
}

combined_sylph_taxprof_data <- sylph_taxprof_results_list %>%
  keep(is.data.frame) %>%
  list_rbind()

daemons(0)

if (nrow(combined_sylph_taxprof_data) > 0) {
  message("Uploading to Postgres...")

  dbExecute(pg, 'DROP INDEX IF EXISTS public.sylph_taxprof_sample')
  dbExecute(pg, 'DROP INDEX IF EXISTS public.sylph_taxprof_rank')
  dbExecute(pg, 'DROP INDEX IF EXISTS public.sylph_taxprof_taxon')

  dbWriteTable(pg, sylph_taxprof_table, combined_sylph_taxprof_data, append = TRUE, row.names = FALSE)

  dbExecute(pg, str_glue('CREATE INDEX "sylph_taxprof_sample" ON "{sylph_taxprof_table}" ("sample")'))
  dbExecute(pg, str_glue('CREATE INDEX "sylph_taxprof_rank" ON "{sylph_taxprof_table}" ("rank")'))
  dbExecute(pg, str_glue('CREATE INDEX "sylph_taxprof_taxon" ON "{sylph_taxprof_table}" ("taxon")'))

  message("Success!")
}
```


# UniRef mapping to genes with Diamond
```{r}
diamond_uniref_contig_mapping <- tbl(pg, "diamond_uniref_contig_mapping")

diamond_mapped_samples <- get_pg_table_samples(pg, "diamond_uniref_contig_mapping", "sample")

uniref_contig_mappings <- Sys.glob("data/omics/metagenomes/*/*_GENES.m8") %>% 
  data.frame(path = .) %>% 
  mutate(sample = basename(path) %>% str_remove("_GENES.m8"))

new_uniref_contig_mappings <- uniref_contig_mappings %>% 
  filter(!sample %in% diamond_mapped_samples$sample)

read_uniref_contig_mapping <- function(path, sample_name){
  cols <- c("qseqid", "qlen", "sseqid", "slen", "qstart", "qend", "sstart", "send", "evalue", "pident", "mismatch", "qcovhsp", "scovhsp")
  
  mapping_res <- read_tsv(path,col_names = cols,show_col_types = FALSE) %>% 
    mutate(uniref100_id = str_remove(sseqid, "UniRef100_"),
           sample = sample_name)
  
  # Only used when creating the table for the first time, for all subsequent additions, append = TRUE should be added and the field types are already established
  postgres_col_types = c(qlen = 'integer',
                            slen = 'integer',
                            qstart = 'integer',
                            qend = 'integer',
                            sstart = 'integer',
                            send = 'integer',
                            pident = 'real',
                            mismatch = 'integer',
                            qcovhsp = 'real',
                            scovhsp = 'real',
                            evalue = 'numeric')
  
  # First run to create table
  # dbWriteTable(pg,"diamond_uniref_contig_mapping",mapping_res,overwrite = FALSE, field.types = postgres_col_types)
  
  # For appending new samples
  dbWriteTable(pg,"diamond_uniref_contig_mapping",mapping_res,overwrite = FALSE, append = TRUE)
  
  return(NULL)
}

walk2(new_uniref_contig_mappings$path, new_uniref_contig_mappings$sample, read_uniref_contig_mapping,.progress = TRUE)
```

```{r}
read_mapping_LCA_summary <- tbl(pg, "read_mapping_LCA_summary")

mapped_samples <- get_pg_table_samples(pg, "read_mapping_LCA_summary", "SampleID")

# mapped_samples <- mmseqs_uniref_mapping %>%

#   distinct() %>% 
#   collect() %>% 
#   pull("sample")

uniref_LCA_reports <- Sys.glob("data/omics/metagenomes/*/*_report_w_standardized_lineage") %>% 
  data.frame(path = .) %>% 
  unglue::unglue_unnest(path, "data/omics/metagenomes/{sample}/{sample2}_report_w_standardized_lineage",remove = FALSE)

new_uniref_LCA_reports <- uniref_LCA_reports %>% 
  filter(!sample %in% mapped_samples$sample,
         sample2 == sample, # some dirs also hold an older report named by the original sample name
         str_detect(sample, "^samp_*")) %>%
  mutate(fs::file_info(path))

#tax_of_interest <- googlesheets4::read_sheet("https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1izMOKyA6ecy2lZsXLoXGnftcyFDdlQI39ncUXnfDw_Y/edit#gid=0")

read_report <- function(path, samp_name){
  cols <- c("percent_and_below", "count_and_below", "count_directly", "rank", "tax_id", "tax_name", "lineage_full", "lineage_std")
  levels <- c("Kingdom", "Phylum", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus", "Species")
  
  report <- data.table::fread(path, col.names = cols) %>% 
    select(-count_directly, -count_and_below) %>% 
    dplyr::rename(percent_abundance = "percent_and_below") %>% 
    mutate(SampleID = samp_name) %>% 
    separate(lineage_std, into = levels, sep = ";[A-z]__", remove = FALSE) %>% 
    mutate(Kingdom = str_remove(Kingdom,"k__"))
  
  dbWriteTable(pg,"read_mapping_LCA_summary",report,overwrite = FALSE, append = TRUE)
  
  return(NULL)
}
```

## GTDB (versioned)
```{r}
# GTDB-Tk gets periodically re-run against newer GTDB releases (see rule GTDB_r232 in the
# Snakefile). Unlike the legacy `GTDB` table above (which only ever holds r207 results),
# this table carries the release alongside every row so multiple releases can coexist.
gtdb_release <- "r232"
gtdb_out_dir <- "GTDB_r232"  # matches params$out_dir basename in rule GTDB_r232
gtdb_table <- "GTDB_versioned"

# Dedup key is (sample, gtdb_marker_set), not just sample: a sample's bins are classified
# into a bac120 and/or an ar53 summary file, and those files don't always land in the same
# run, so deduping on `sample` alone risks never loading a later-arriving file.
if (DBI::dbExistsTable(pg, gtdb_table)) {
  existing_gtdb_versioned <- tbl(pg, gtdb_table) %>%
    filter(gtdb_release == .env$gtdb_release) %>%
    select(sample, gtdb_marker_set) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    collect()
} else {
  existing_gtdb_versioned <- tibble(sample = character(), gtdb_marker_set = character())
}

# Find all GTDB_r232 summary tsvs
GTDB_versioned_paths <- Sys.glob(str_glue("data/omics/metagenomes/*/bins/{gtdb_out_dir}/*.summary.tsv")) %>%
  data.frame(path = .) %>%
  bind_cols(., unglue::unglue_data(.$path, str_glue("data/omics/{{sample_type}}/{{sample}}/bins/{gtdb_out_dir}/gtdbtk.{{gtdb_marker_set}}.summary.tsv"))) %>%
  bind_cols(file.info(.$path))

# Filter list of summary tsvs to only those not already loaded into the database
new_GTDB_versioned <- GTDB_versioned_paths %>%
  anti_join(existing_gtdb_versioned, by = c("sample", "gtdb_marker_set")) %>%
  filter(str_detect(sample, "^samp_") | str_detect(sample, "^coassembly_") | str_detect(sample, "^GVHDsamp_"))

# Initialize the mirai cluster for parallel tsv parsing prior to upload
n_cores <- parallel::detectCores() - 1
daemons(n_cores)

message(paste("Processing", nrow(new_GTDB_versioned), "GTDB_r232 summary files across", n_cores, "cores..."))

# everywhere() only evaluates in the daemon processes (never in this calling session), so it
# is used solely to load packages remotely; the worker function itself must be a real object
# in this session for mirai_map() to find and ship it.
everywhere({
  library(dplyr)
  library(readr)
  library(stringr)
  library(tidyr)
})

# Read every column as character here -- some summary.tsv files have entirely-NA numeric
# columns (e.g. closest_placement_* when no placement was found, or most columns in an
# ar53 file with only a couple of archaeal bins), which makes readr infer col_logical()
# for that file. Reading everything as character sidesteps per-file type drift so
# list_rbind() across hundreds of files never hits a type clash; real types are cast once
# below via type_convert(), after all files are combined.
read_gtdb_versioned_parallel <- function(path, sample, gtdb_marker_set, gtdb_release) {
  tryCatch({
    read_tsv(path, na = "N/A", col_types = cols(.default = col_character())) %>%
      separate(classification, into = c("domain","phylum","class","order","family","genus","species"), sep = ";[a-z]__", remove = FALSE) %>%
      mutate(domain = str_remove(domain, "d__"),
             sample = sample,
             gtdb_marker_set = gtdb_marker_set,
             gtdb_release = gtdb_release) %>%
      dplyr::rename(bin = "user_genome") %>%
      relocate(gtdb_release, sample, bin, gtdb_marker_set)
  }, error = function(e) return(conditionMessage(e)))
}

combined_gtdb_versioned_results <- mirai_map(
  .x = new_GTDB_versioned %>% select(path, sample, gtdb_marker_set),
  .f = read_gtdb_versioned_parallel,
  .args = list(gtdb_release = gtdb_release)
)

# Cast numeric columns once, over the combined data, to match the existing GTDB table's
# postgres types exactly (double precision for these 9 columns; text -- the .default -- for
# everything else, including the new gtdb_release/gtdb_marker_set columns).
combined_gtdb_versioned_data <- combined_gtdb_versioned_results[] %>%
  list_rbind() %>%
  type_convert(col_types = cols(
    closest_genome_reference_radius = col_double(),
    closest_genome_ani = col_double(),
    closest_genome_af = col_double(),
    closest_placement_radius = col_double(),
    closest_placement_ani = col_double(),
    closest_placement_af = col_double(),
    msa_percent = col_double(),
    translation_table = col_double(),
    red_value = col_double(),
    .default = col_character()
  ))

daemons(0)

if (nrow(combined_gtdb_versioned_data) > 0) {
  message("Uploading to Postgres...")

  dbExecute(pg, 'DROP INDEX IF EXISTS public.gtdb_versioned_release')
  dbExecute(pg, 'DROP INDEX IF EXISTS public.gtdb_versioned_sample')
  dbExecute(pg, 'DROP INDEX IF EXISTS public.gtdb_versioned_bin')

  dbWriteTable(pg, gtdb_table, combined_gtdb_versioned_data, append = TRUE, row.names = FALSE)

  dbExecute(pg, str_glue('CREATE INDEX "gtdb_versioned_release" ON "{gtdb_table}" ("gtdb_release")'))
  dbExecute(pg, str_glue('CREATE INDEX "gtdb_versioned_sample" ON "{gtdb_table}" ("sample")'))
  dbExecute(pg, str_glue('CREATE INDEX "gtdb_versioned_bin" ON "{gtdb_table}" ("bin")'))

  message("Success!")
}
```

## GTDB to NCBI taxonomy
```{r}
# Rule GTDB_to_NCBI runs gtdb_to_ncbi_majority_vote.py over the GTDB-Tk output, translating each
# bin's GTDB classification into a majority-vote NCBI classification. Like the versioned GTDB
# table above, the release is carried on every row so multiple releases can coexist; pointing
# this at another release is just a change to the two variables below.
gtdb_ncbi_release <- "r232"
gtdb_ncbi_out_dir <- "GTDB_r232"  # matches params$out_dir basename in rule GTDB_to_NCBI
gtdb_ncbi_table <- "gtdb_to_ncbi"

# Guarded because the table doesn't exist until the first successful load
if (DBI::dbExistsTable(pg, gtdb_ncbi_table)) {
  existing_gtdb_to_ncbi <- tbl(pg, gtdb_ncbi_table) %>%
    filter(gtdb_release == .env$gtdb_ncbi_release) %>%
    select(sample) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    collect()
} else {
  existing_gtdb_to_ncbi <- tibble(sample = character())
}

# Find all gtdb_to_ncbi results
gtdb_to_ncbi_paths <- Sys.glob(str_glue("data/omics/metagenomes/*/bins/{gtdb_ncbi_out_dir}/gtdb_to_ncbi_taxonmy.tsv")) %>%
  data.frame(path = .) %>%
  bind_cols(., unglue::unglue_data(.$path, str_glue("data/omics/{{sample_type}}/{{sample}}/bins/{gtdb_ncbi_out_dir}/gtdb_to_ncbi_taxonmy.tsv"))) %>%
  bind_cols(file.info(.$path))

# Filter to only those not already loaded into the database
new_gtdb_to_ncbi <- gtdb_to_ncbi_paths %>%
  filter(!sample %in% existing_gtdb_to_ncbi$sample,
         str_detect(sample, "^samp_") | str_detect(sample, "^coassembly_") | str_detect(sample, "^GVHDsamp_"))

# Initialize the mirai cluster for parallel tsv parsing prior to upload
n_cores <- parallel::detectCores() - 1
daemons(n_cores)

message(paste("Processing", nrow(new_gtdb_to_ncbi), "gtdb_to_ncbi files across", n_cores, "cores..."))

everywhere({
  library(dplyr)
  library(readr)
  library(stringr)
  library(tidyr)
})

# All three columns are text, so no type inference/casting is needed after binding.
read_gtdb_to_ncbi_parallel <- function(path, sample, gtdb_release) {
  tryCatch({
    read_tsv(path, col_types = cols(.default = col_character())) %>%
      dplyr::rename(bin = "Genome ID",
                    gtdb_classification = "GTDB classification",
                    ncbi_classification = "Majority vote NCBI classification") %>%
      # fill = "right" because bins the majority vote couldn't place come through as a bare
      # "Unclassified"/"Unclassified Bacteria" with no rank prefixes at all; those get the string
      # in ncbi_domain and NA for the remaining ranks instead of a warning per file.
      separate(ncbi_classification,
               into = c("ncbi_domain","ncbi_phylum","ncbi_class","ncbi_order","ncbi_family","ncbi_genus","ncbi_species"),
               sep = ";[a-z]__", remove = FALSE, fill = "right") %>%
      mutate(ncbi_domain = str_remove(ncbi_domain, "d__"),
             sample = sample,
             gtdb_release = gtdb_release) %>%
      relocate(gtdb_release, sample, bin)
  }, error = function(e) return(conditionMessage(e)))
}

combined_gtdb_to_ncbi_results <- mirai_map(
  .x = new_gtdb_to_ncbi %>% select(path, sample),
  .f = read_gtdb_to_ncbi_parallel,
  .args = list(gtdb_release = gtdb_ncbi_release)
)

# This waits for all workers to finish and binds the resulting data frames
combined_gtdb_to_ncbi_data <- combined_gtdb_to_ncbi_results[] %>%
  list_rbind()

daemons(0)

if (nrow(combined_gtdb_to_ncbi_data) > 0) {
  message("Uploading to Postgres...")

  dbExecute(pg, 'DROP INDEX IF EXISTS public.gtdb_to_ncbi_release')
  dbExecute(pg, 'DROP INDEX IF EXISTS public.gtdb_to_ncbi_sample')
  dbExecute(pg, 'DROP INDEX IF EXISTS public.gtdb_to_ncbi_bin')

  dbWriteTable(pg, gtdb_ncbi_table, combined_gtdb_to_ncbi_data, append = TRUE, row.names = FALSE)

  dbExecute(pg, str_glue('CREATE INDEX "gtdb_to_ncbi_release" ON "{gtdb_ncbi_table}" ("gtdb_release")'))
  dbExecute(pg, str_glue('CREATE INDEX "gtdb_to_ncbi_sample" ON "{gtdb_ncbi_table}" ("sample")'))
  dbExecute(pg, str_glue('CREATE INDEX "gtdb_to_ncbi_bin" ON "{gtdb_ncbi_table}" ("bin")'))

  message("Success!")
}
```

## DREP
```{r}
# Get DREP results that are already loaded into the database
existing_drep_annotations <- tbl(pg, "drep") %>% 
  select(sample) %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  collect() 

# Find all DREP results
drep_paths <- Sys.glob("data/omics/metagenomes/*/bins/drep/data_tables/Cdb.csv") %>% 
  data.frame(path = .) %>% 
  bind_cols(.,unglue::unglue_data(.$path,"data/omics/{sample_type}/{sample}/bins/drep/data_tables/Cdb.csv")) %>% 
  bind_cols(file.info(.$path))

# Filter list of summary tsvs to only those not already loaded into the database
new_drep <- drep_paths %>% 
  filter(
      !sample %in% existing_drep_annotations$sample,
      (str_detect(sample, "^samp_") | str_detect(sample, "^coassembly_") | str_detect(sample, "^GVHDsamp_")))

# Initialize the mirai cluster for parallel csv parsing prior to upload
# Use parallel::detectCores() - 1 to leave a core for the OS
library(mirai)
n_cores <- parallel::detectCores() - 1
daemons(n_cores)

# Execute in Parallel
message(paste("Processing", nrow(new_drep), "samples across", n_cores, "cores..."))

everywhere({
  library(dplyr)
  library(readr)
  library(stringr)
  library(fs)
  
  read_drep_parallel <- function(path, sample) {
    tryCatch({
      scores_path <- stringr::str_replace(path, 'Cdb.csv', 'Sdb.csv')
      
      scores <- readr::read_csv(scores_path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>% 
        dplyr::rename(drep_score = "score")
      
      df <- readr::read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
        dplyr::left_join(scores, by = "genome") %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(
          drep_folder = stringr::str_remove(path, '/data_tables/Cdb.csv'),
          is_cluster_rep = fs::file_exists(stringr::str_glue("{drep_folder}/dereplicated_genomes/{genome}")),
          genome = stringr::str_remove(genome, ".fa"),
          sample = sample
        ) %>% 
        dplyr::rename(bin = "genome") %>% 
        dplyr::select(-drep_folder) %>% 
        dplyr::relocate(sample)
      
      return(df)
    }, error = function(e) return(conditionMessage(e)))
  }
})


combined_drep_results <- mirai_map(
  .x = new_drep %>% select(path,sample), 
  .f = read_drep_parallel
)

# This waits for all workers to finish and binds the resulting data frames
combined_drep_data <-  combined_drep_results[] %>% 
  list_rbind()

# Shut down daemons once data is collected
daemons(0)

# Database Upload
if (nrow(combined_drep_data) > 0) {
  message("Uploading to Postgres...")
  
  # Clean up indices before bulk load
  dbExecute(pg, 'DROP INDEX IF EXISTS public.drep_bin')
  dbExecute(pg, 'DROP INDEX IF EXISTS public.drep_rep')
  dbExecute(pg, 'DROP INDEX IF EXISTS public.drep_cluster')
  dbExecute(pg, 'DROP INDEX IF EXISTS public.drep_sample')

  dbWriteTable(pg, "drep", combined_drep_data, append = TRUE, row.names = FALSE)

  # Recreate indices
  dbExecute(pg, 'CREATE INDEX "drep_bin" ON "drep" ("bin")')
  dbExecute(pg, 'CREATE INDEX "drep_rep" ON "drep" ("is_cluster_rep")')
  dbExecute(pg, 'CREATE INDEX "drep_cluster" ON "drep" ("secondary_cluster")')
  dbExecute(pg, 'CREATE INDEX "drep_sample" ON "drep" ("sample")')
  
  message("Success!")
}
```

# Gene abundance results

```{r}
gene_abundance <- tbl(pg, "gene_abundance")

gene_abundance_samples <- get_pg_table_samples(pg, "gene_abundance", "sample")

gene_abundance_files <- Sys.glob(c("data/omics/metagenomes/*/genes/*_READSvsGENES.rpkm",
                                   "data/omics/metatranscriptomes/*/genes/*_READSvsGENES.rpkm")) %>%
  data.frame(path = .) %>%
  unglue::unglue_unnest(path, "data/omics/{sample_type}/{sample}/genes/{sample2}_READSvsGENES.rpkm",remove = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(file_size = fs::file_size(path))

# metaT assemblies get re-run (e.g. the Oct 2026 RNAspades re-assembly on rRNA-removed reads); an rpkm
# file older than its assembly has gene/contig IDs from the old assembly, so skip it until it's rebuilt
metaT_assembly <- function(sample) str_glue("data/omics/metatranscriptomes/{sample}/assembly/RNAspades/contigs.renamed.fasta")

new_gene_abundance_files <- gene_abundance_files %>%
  filter(!sample %in% gene_abundance_samples$sample,
         str_detect(sample, "^samp_*") | str_detect(sample, "^coassembly_*") | str_detect(sample, "^GVHDsamp_")) %>%
  filter(sample_type != "metatranscriptomes" |
           (file.exists(metaT_assembly(sample)) & fs::file_info(path)$modification_time > fs::file_info(metaT_assembly(sample))$modification_time)) %>%
  mutate(fs::file_info(path))

#path <- "data/omics/metagenomes/samp_447/genes/samp_447_READSvsGENES.rpkm"
#sample_name = "samp_447"

read_gene_abundance <- function(path, sample_name){
  
  gene_abund_df <- read_tsv(path,skip = 4,show_col_types = FALSE) %>% 
    dplyr::rename(gene_header = "#Name") %>% 
    mutate(tpm = (FPKM / sum(FPKM))*10^6) %>% 
    separate(gene_header, into = c("gene", "left_edge","right_edge", "strand", "id"),sep = " # ") %>% 
    separate(id, into = c("id", "partial","start_type", "rbs_motif", "rbs_spacer","gc_content"), sep = ";") %>% 
    mutate(across(c("id", "partial","start_type", "rbs_motif", "rbs_spacer","gc_content"), ~str_remove(.x, "^.*="))) %>% 
    separate(id, into = c("contig_num", "gene_num"), sep = "_",remove = FALSE) %>% 
    mutate(sample = sample_name,
           contig = str_glue("{sample}_{contig_num}")) %>% 
    type_convert() %>% 
    dplyr::rename(length = "Length", bases = "Bases", coverage = "Coverage", reads = "Reads", rpkm = "RPKM", frags = "Frags", fpkm = "FPKM") %>% 
    relocate(gene, contig, sample) %>% 
    dplyr::select(-id)

  
  
  
  # Only used when creating the table for the first time, for all subsequent additions,
  # append = TRUE should be added as the field types are already established
  postgres_col_types = c(gene = 'text',
                         sample = "text",
                         contig = "text",
                         contig_num = "bigint",
                         gene_num = "int",
                         left_edge = 'bigint',
                         right_edge = 'bigint',
                         strand = "integer",
                         partial = "text",
                         start_type = "text",
                         rbs_motif = "text",
                         rbs_spacer = "text",
                         gc_content = "numeric",
                         length = "integer",
                         bases = "bigint",
                         coverage = "numeric",
                         reads = "bigint",
                         rpkm = "numeric",
                         frags = "bigint",
                         fpkm = "numeric",
                         tpm = "numeric")

  # # First run to create table
   # dbWriteTable(conn = pg,
   #              name = "gene_abundance",
   #              gene_abund_df,
   #              overwrite = FALSE,
   #              field.types = postgres_col_types)

  dbWriteTable(conn = pg,
               name = "gene_abundance",
               value = gene_abund_df,
               overwrite = FALSE, append = TRUE)
  
  return(NULL)
}

# Indexes are left in place while appending: the table is ~2.5 billion rows, so rebuilding them takes
# hours, while a typical batch of new samples appends fine with them maintained. (The live indexes are
# idx_gene_abundance_{sample,gene,contig} plus gene_abundance_sample; the old drop/create lines here
# targeted names that no longer exist.) For a very large first load, drop and recreate those instead.
walk2(new_gene_abundance_files$path, new_gene_abundance_files$sample, read_gene_abundance,.progress = TRUE)

```

cleanup kofamscan table, remove low qual hits unlikely to be of interst
```{r}

kofam_index_task <- mirai({
  # Open a local connection inside the worker
  worker_pg <- DBI::dbConnect(
    RPostgres::Postgres(), 
    dbname = "glamr_data", 
    host = "cayman.earth.lsa.umich.edu", 
    port = "5432", 
    user = "glamr_admin", 
    password = "glamr2023"
  )

  # 2. Define the SQL Query to keep only the top 5 hits per gene
  # Note: ctid is a system column in Postgres; if you have a primary key (e.g., 'id'), use that instead.
  sql_cleanup <- "
    CREATE TABLE public.kofam_scan_new AS
    SELECT gene, sample, sig, ko, thrshld, score, e_value
    FROM (
        SELECT *, 
               ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
                   PARTITION BY gene 
                   ORDER BY score DESC
               ) as rank
        FROM public.kofam_scan
        WHERE sig = true OR e_value < 0.01
    ) ranked
    WHERE rank <= 5;"

  message("Running cleanup: Keeping top 5 hits per gene...")
  rows_affected <- DBI::dbExecute(worker_pg, sql_cleanup)
  
  # Disconnect
  DBI::dbDisconnect(worker_pg)
  
  return(paste("Task complete. Rows modified:", rows_affected))
})

# Immediate feedback in main R session
message("The kofam_scan indices and hit-reduction query are running in the background...")

# Check status (TRUE = still running)
unresolved(kofam_index_task)


```



### KOFAMscan sig hits using the anvio heurisitic
```{r}

kofam_scan_pg <- tbl(pg, "kofam_scan")

kofam_sig_anvio <- kofam_scan_pg %>% 
  group_by(gene, ko) %>% 
  mutate(mod_threshold = 0.5 * thrshld) %>% 
  filter(score > mod_threshold,
         e_value < 1e-05) %>% 
  slice_max(score) %>% 
  group_by(gene) %>% 
  mutate(n_relaxed_hits = n()) %>% 
  filter(n_relaxed_hits == 1 | sig == TRUE) %>% 
  mutate(sig_relaxed = TRUE) %>% 
  slice_max(score) %>% 
  slice_max(thrshld, with_ties = FALSE) %>% # break gene score ties by picking the gene with the higher threshold
  show_query()



```


```{r}
library(mirai)

# 1. Dispatch the task to a background worker
kofam_mv_task <- mirai({
  # Open a local connection inside the worker
  worker_pg <- DBI::dbConnect(
    RPostgres::Postgres(), 
    dbname = "glamr_data", 
    host = "cayman.earth.lsa.umich.edu", 
    port = "5432", 
    user = "glamr_admin", 
    password = "glamr2023"
  )

  # Define the SQL for the Materialized View
  sql_mv <- "
    CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW public.kofam_scan_signif_anvio
    TABLESPACE pg_default
    AS SELECT gene,
        sample,
        sig,
        ko,
        thrshld,
        score,
        e_value,
        mod_threshold,
        n_relaxed_hits,
        sig_relaxed
       FROM ( SELECT q01_1.gene,
                q01_1.sample,
                q01_1.sig,
                q01_1.ko,
                q01_1.thrshld,
                q01_1.score,
                q01_1.e_value,
                q01_1.mod_threshold,
                q01_1.n_relaxed_hits,
                q01_1.sig_relaxed,
                row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY q01_1.gene ORDER BY q01_1.thrshld DESC) AS col03
               FROM ( SELECT q01_2.gene,
                        q01_2.sample,
                        q01_2.sig,
                        q01_2.ko,
                        q01_2.thrshld,
                        q01_2.score,
                        q01_2.e_value,
                        q01_2.mod_threshold,
                        q01_2.n_relaxed_hits,
                        q01_2.sig_relaxed,
                        rank() OVER (PARTITION BY q01_2.gene ORDER BY q01_2.score DESC) AS col02
                       FROM ( SELECT q01_3.gene,
                                q01_3.sample,
                                q01_3.sig,
                                q01_3.ko,
                                q01_3.thrshld,
                                q01_3.score,
                                q01_3.e_value,
                                q01_3.mod_threshold,
                                q01_3.n_relaxed_hits,
                                true AS sig_relaxed
                               FROM ( SELECT q01_4.gene,
                                        q01_4.sample,
                                        q01_4.sig,
                                        q01_4.ko,
                                        q01_4.thrshld,
                                        q01_4.score,
                                        q01_4.e_value,
                                        q01_4.mod_threshold,
                                        count(*) OVER (PARTITION BY q01_4.gene) AS n_relaxed_hits
                                       FROM ( SELECT q01_5.gene,
        q01_5.sample,
        q01_5.sig,
        q01_5.ko,
        q01_5.thrshld,
        q01_5.score,
        q01_5.e_value,
        q01_5.mod_threshold,
        rank() OVER (PARTITION BY q01_5.gene, q01_5.ko ORDER BY q01_5.score DESC) AS col01
       FROM ( SELECT kofam_scan.gene,
          kofam_scan.sample,
          kofam_scan.sig,
          kofam_scan.ko,
          kofam_scan.thrshld,
          kofam_scan.score,
          kofam_scan.e_value,
          0.5 * kofam_scan.thrshld AS mod_threshold
         FROM kofam_scan) q01_5
      WHERE q01_5.score > q01_5.mod_threshold AND q01_5.e_value < 0.00001) q01_4
                                      WHERE q01_4.col01 <= 1) q01_3
                              WHERE q01_3.n_relaxed_hits::numeric = 1.0 OR q01_3.sig = true) q01_2) q01_1
              WHERE q01_1.col02 <= 1) q01
      WHERE col03 <= 1
    WITH DATA;"
    
  
  # Define Index Queries
  sql_idx1 <- "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_kofam_scan_signif_anvio_gene_unique ON public.kofam_scan_signif_anvio (gene);"
  sql_idx2 <- "CREATE INDEX idx_kofam_scan_signif_anvio_ko ON public.kofam_scan_signif_anvio (ko);"
  sql_idx3 <- "CREATE INDEX idx_kofam_scan_signif_anvio_sample ON public.kofam_scan_signif_anvio (sample);"

  # Execute sequence
  message("Creating Materialized View...")
  DBI::dbExecute(worker_pg, sql_mv)
  
  message("Creating Indexes...")
  DBI::dbExecute(worker_pg, sql_idx1)
  DBI::dbExecute(worker_pg, sql_idx2)
  DBI::dbExecute(worker_pg, sql_idx3)

  # Disconnect
  DBI::dbDisconnect(worker_pg)
  
  return("Materialized view and indexes created successfully.")
})

# 2. Immediate feedback in main R session
message("The Materialized View creation is running in the background...")

# 3. Monitor status
 unresolved(kofam_mv_task)  # Returns TRUE if still working
 kofam_mv_task$data         # Access the return message once finished
```

The index creation above never actually completed -- the materialized view existed with
no indexes at all, so every `WHERE sample = ...` was a parallel sequential scan of the
whole 62 GB view (481M rows, 8.1M pages).

A BRIN index is a much better fit here than the btree originally attempted. The view is
built with `row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY gene ...)`, which leaves it physically sorted
by gene, and gene ids start with the sample name -- so `pg_stats` reports a correlation of
0.99998 on `sample`. BRIN stores only per-block-range min/max, which is why it costs 11 MB
and 2.5 minutes instead of ~15 GB and several hours.

```{r}
pg <- DBI::dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(),dbname = "glamr_data", host = "cayman.earth.lsa.umich.edu", port = "5432", user = "glamr_admin", password = "glamr2023")

dbExecute(pg, "CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_kofam_signif_anvio_sample_brin
                 ON public.kofam_scan_signif_anvio USING brin (sample)
                 WITH (pages_per_range = 32)")   # 2m22s, 11 MB

dbExecute(pg, "ANALYZE public.kofam_scan_signif_anvio")   # 32s

# Confirm the plan is a Bitmap Heap Scan rather than a Seq Scan.
# Measured: 6.4s for a sample returning 408k rows (was an 8.8M-cost seq scan).
dbGetQuery(pg, "EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)
                  SELECT gene, ko FROM kofam_scan_signif_anvio WHERE sample = 'GVHDsamp_1'")
```

The `(gene)` and `(ko)` indexes from the chunk above are deliberately still absent -- nothing
queries the view that way, and the `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... (gene)` is the most likely reason
the original background task died partway through.

See `code/kegg_completeness_funcs.R`, which depends on this index; its
`check_kegg_completeness_prereqs()` verifies the plan contains no `Seq Scan` before running.


kofam significant hit table
```{r}

library(mirai)

# Dispatch the task with "IF EXISTS" guards
kofam_sig_view_task <- mirai({
  # Open connection inside worker
  worker_pg <- DBI::dbConnect(
    RPostgres::Postgres(), 
    dbname = "glamr_data", 
    host = "cayman.earth.lsa.umich.edu", 
    port = "5432", 
    user = "glamr_admin", 
    password = "glamr2023"
  )

  # 1. Drop existing view and indexes if they already exist
  # Note: Dropping the MV automatically drops its associated indexes
  sql_drop <- "DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW IF EXISTS public.kofam_scan_signif CASCADE;"

  # 2. Define the SQL exactly as provided
  sql_view <- "
    CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW public.kofam_scan_signif
    TABLESPACE pg_default
    AS SELECT gene,
        ko,
        sample
       FROM kofam_scan
      WHERE sig = true
    WITH DATA;"

  sql_idx_gene <- "CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_kofam_scan_sig_gene ON public.kofam_scan_signif USING btree (gene);"
  sql_idx_uniq <- "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_kofam_scan_sig_unique ON public.kofam_scan_signif USING btree (gene, ko, sample);"

  # Execute sequence
  message("Cleaning up old view if it exists...")
  DBI::dbExecute(worker_pg, sql_drop)
  
  message("Creating Materialized View: kofam_scan_signif...")
  DBI::dbExecute(worker_pg, sql_view)
  
  message("Creating Indexes for kofam_scan_signif...")
  DBI::dbExecute(worker_pg, sql_idx_gene)
  DBI::dbExecute(worker_pg, sql_idx_uniq)

  # Disconnect
  DBI::dbDisconnect(worker_pg)
  
  return("Task complete: kofam_scan_signif (re)created with indexes.")
})

# Immediate feedback in main R session
message("The kofam_scan_signif view creation (with IF EXISTS guards) is running...")

unresolved(kofam_sig_view_task)
```

# eggNOG-mapper
```{r eggnog}
# Rule eggnog writes data/omics/{sample_type}/{sample}/eggnog/{sample}.emapper.annotations.
# Loaded as two tables joined on gene:
#   eggnog: one row per gene with the single-valued fields (seed ortholog, hit stats, preferred name)
#   eggnog_annotations: long format, one row per gene and annotation value (KO, EC, GO, PFAM, ...),
#     with annotation types stored as smallint ids described in eggnog_annotation_types
#
# The annotation_confidence column of the .emapper.annotations file is a positional string with one
# h/m/l/- character per field (Preferred_name, GOs, EC, KEGG_ko, KEGG_Pathway, KEGG_Module,
# KEGG_Reaction, KEGG_rclass, BRITE, KEGG_TC, CAZy, BiGG_Reaction, PFAMs). It is split up so each
# eggnog_annotations row carries the confidence of its own annotation (NULL for COG_category and
# eggNOG_OGs, which have none) and preferred_name_confidence is kept on the eggnog row.
#
# The files in the GVHD sample folders are symlinks into another turbo volume, so when running in the
# r_microbiome container it needs --bind /nfs:/nfs or those samples are silently not found.
eggnog_table <- "eggnog"
eggnog_annot_table <- "eggnog_annotations"

# Optionally limit loading to specific samples, NULL loads every sample with eggnog results
eggnog_samples_to_load <- NULL # e.g. c("samp_2053", "samp_7915")

# Workers write directly to the database, keep this modest so the server isn't overwhelmed
n_eggnog_workers <- 8

# Index builds on these tables take hours. FALSE only prints the SQL, to run it with psql on the
# database host (a dropped tunnel connection kills a build run from here).
eggnog_run_index_sql <- TRUE

eggnog_annotation_types <- tibble(
  annotation_type = c("KEGG_ko", "EC", "GOs", "PFAMs", "COG_category", "KEGG_Pathway", "KEGG_Module",
                      "KEGG_Reaction", "KEGG_rclass", "BRITE", "KEGG_TC", "CAZy", "BiGG_Reaction", "eggNOG_OGs")) %>%
  mutate(annotation_type_id = row_number(), .before = 1)

# Order of the characters in the annotation_confidence string
eggnog_confidence_order <- c("Preferred_name", "GOs", "EC", "KEGG_ko", "KEGG_Pathway", "KEGG_Module",
                             "KEGG_Reaction", "KEGG_rclass", "BRITE", "KEGG_TC", "CAZy", "BiGG_Reaction", "PFAMs")

# Create the tables on the first run with explicit types
if (!DBI::dbExistsTable(pg, "eggnog_annotation_types")) {
  dbWriteTable(pg, "eggnog_annotation_types", eggnog_annotation_types,
               field.types = c(annotation_type_id = "smallint", annotation_type = "text"))
}
if (!DBI::dbExistsTable(pg, eggnog_table)) {
  dbExecute(pg, str_glue('CREATE TABLE "{eggnog_table}" (
    gene text, sample text, seed_ortholog text, evalue double precision,
    score double precision, tax_ceiling text, farthest_donor_lineage text, preferred_name text,
    preferred_name_confidence "char")'))
  # extra holds the PFAM domain coordinates (start_end), split off of the PFAM name
  # confidence is eggnog-mapper\'s h/m/l (high/medium/low) for the annotation
  dbExecute(pg, str_glue('CREATE TABLE "{eggnog_annot_table}" (
    gene text, sample text, annotation_type_id smallint, value text, extra text, confidence "char")'))
}

eggnog_samples <- get_pg_table_samples(pg, eggnog_table, "sample")

# Find all eggnog annotation files
eggnog_files <- Sys.glob("data/omics/*/*/eggnog/*.emapper.annotations") %>%
  data.frame(path = .) %>%
  bind_cols(., unglue::unglue_data(.$path, "data/omics/{sample_type}/{sample}/eggnog/{sample2}.emapper.annotations")) %>%
  filter(sample == sample2) %>%
  select(-sample2)

if (!is.null(eggnog_samples_to_load)) {
  eggnog_files <- eggnog_files %>%
    filter(sample %in% eggnog_samples_to_load)
}

# Filter to only those not already loaded into the database
new_eggnog_files <- eggnog_files %>%
  filter(!sample %in% eggnog_samples$sample,
         str_detect(sample, "^samp_") | str_detect(sample, "^coassembly_") | str_detect(sample, "^GVHDsamp_"))

# Each worker parses one sample and writes both tables in a single transaction, so a sample
# is either fully loaded or not at all and an interrupted load can simply be re-run
load_eggnog_parallel <- function(path, sample, eggnog_table, eggnog_annot_table, annotation_types, confidence_order) {
  tryCatch({
    # The annotations file is written incrementally, only completed runs end with the timing footer
    if (!any(str_detect(system2("tail", c("-n", "3", shQuote(path)), stdout = TRUE), "^## Total time"))) {
      return("incomplete annotations file (no '## Total time' footer)")
    }

    col_names <- c("gene", "seed_ortholog", "evalue", "score", "eggNOG_OGs", "tax_ceiling",
                   "farthest_donor_lineage", "COG_category", "preferred_name", "GOs", "EC", "KEGG_ko",
                   "KEGG_Pathway", "KEGG_Module", "KEGG_Reaction", "KEGG_rclass", "BRITE", "KEGG_TC",
                   "CAZy", "BiGG_Reaction", "PFAMs", "annotation_confidence")

    # eggnog uses "-" for empty fields
    annot <- read_tsv(pipe(str_glue("grep -v '^#' {shQuote(path)}")), col_names = col_names,
                      col_types = cols(.default = "c", evalue = "d", score = "d"),
                      na = c("", "-"), quote = "", progress = FALSE)

    # annotation_confidence has one character per field in confidence_order, "-" where not annotated
    stopifnot(all(nchar(annot$annotation_confidence) == length(confidence_order)))
    confidence_of <- function(field) {
      pos <- match(field, confidence_order)
      if (is.na(pos)) return(rep(NA_character_, nrow(annot)))
      conf <- str_sub(annot$annotation_confidence, pos, pos)
      if_else(conf == "-", NA_character_, conf)
    }

    gene_df <- annot %>%
      transmute(gene, sample = !!sample, seed_ortholog, evalue, score,
                tax_ceiling, farthest_donor_lineage, preferred_name,
                preferred_name_confidence = confidence_of("Preferred_name"))

    # Multi-valued fields are comma separated. PFAMs carry domain coordinates (e.g. DUF262_15_241),
    # CAZy a family description (e.g. GT2|Glycosyltransferase Family 2.), and EC an "ec:" prefix
    annot_long <- annotation_types$annotation_type %>%
      map(\(type) tibble(gene = annot$gene, annotation_type = type, value = annot[[type]],
                         confidence = confidence_of(type))) %>%
      list_rbind() %>%
      filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
      separate_longer_delim(value, ",") %>%
      mutate(extra = if_else(annotation_type == "PFAMs", str_extract(value, "(?<=_)\\d+_\\d+$"), NA_character_),
             value = case_when(annotation_type == "PFAMs" ~ str_remove(value, "_\\d+_\\d+$"),
                               annotation_type == "CAZy" ~ str_remove(value, "\\|.*$"),
                               annotation_type == "EC" ~ str_remove(value, "^ec:"),
                               .default = value),
             sample = !!sample) %>%
      inner_join(annotation_types, by = "annotation_type") %>%
      select(gene, sample, annotation_type_id, value, extra, confidence)

    worker_pg <- DBI::dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(), dbname = "glamr_data", host = "cayman.earth.lsa.umich.edu", port = "5432", user = "glamr_admin", password = "glamr2023")
    on.exit(DBI::dbDisconnect(worker_pg))

    DBI::dbWithTransaction(worker_pg, {
      DBI::dbWriteTable(worker_pg, eggnog_table, gene_df, append = TRUE)
      DBI::dbWriteTable(worker_pg, eggnog_annot_table, annot_long, append = TRUE)
    })

    tibble(sample = sample, genes = nrow(gene_df), annotations = nrow(annot_long))
  }, error = function(e) return(conditionMessage(e)))
}

# Index names follow the table names so a rebuilt copy of the tables can be indexed beside the originals
eggnog_index_sql <- c(
  str_glue('CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "{eggnog_table}_sample" ON "{eggnog_table}" ("sample")'),
  str_glue('CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "{eggnog_table}_gene" ON "{eggnog_table}" ("gene")'),
  # Gene-name lookups (e.g. preferred_name = 'isiA') are otherwise a scan of every gene
  str_glue('CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "{eggnog_table}_preferred_name" ON "{eggnog_table}" ("preferred_name")'),
  # Covering index: "which genes/samples have annotation X (at confidence Y)" is answered without
  # touching the 1.5 TB table
  str_glue('CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "{eggnog_annot_table}_type_value_cov" ON "{eggnog_annot_table}" ("annotation_type_id", "value") INCLUDE ("gene", "sample", "confidence")'),
  str_glue('CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "{eggnog_annot_table}_gene" ON "{eggnog_annot_table}" ("gene")'),
  str_glue('CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "{eggnog_annot_table}_sample" ON "{eggnog_annot_table}" ("sample")'))

daemons(n_eggnog_workers)

message(paste("Loading", nrow(new_eggnog_files), "eggnog annotation files across", n_eggnog_workers, "workers..."))

everywhere({
  library(dplyr)
  library(readr)
  library(stringr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(tibble)
  library(purrr)
  library(DBI)
})

eggnog_load_results <- mirai_map(
  .x = new_eggnog_files %>% select(path, sample),
  .f = load_eggnog_parallel,
  .args = list(eggnog_table = eggnog_table, eggnog_annot_table = eggnog_annot_table,
               annotation_types = eggnog_annotation_types, confidence_order = eggnog_confidence_order)
)

# This waits for all workers to finish
eggnog_load_results_list <- eggnog_load_results[.progress]

daemons(0)

# load_eggnog_parallel returns the error message instead of a data frame when a sample fails
failed_eggnog <- eggnog_load_results_list %>% discard(is.data.frame)
if (length(failed_eggnog) > 0) {
  warning(length(failed_eggnog), " eggnog samples failed to load and were skipped:\n",
          paste(new_eggnog_files$sample[!map_lgl(eggnog_load_results_list, is.data.frame)], unlist(failed_eggnog), sep = ": ", collapse = "\n"))
}

eggnog_loaded <- eggnog_load_results_list %>%
  keep(is.data.frame) %>%
  list_rbind()

message("Loaded ", nrow(eggnog_loaded), " samples: ", sum(eggnog_loaded$genes), " genes, ",
        sum(eggnog_loaded$annotations), " annotations")

# Autovacuum waits for 20% of rows to change by default, far too late for tables this size
for (tbl_name in c(eggnog_table, eggnog_annot_table)) {
  dbExecute(pg, str_glue('ALTER TABLE "{tbl_name}" SET (autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor = 0.01,
    autovacuum_vacuum_insert_scale_factor = 0.02, autovacuum_analyze_scale_factor = 0.01)'))
}

if (eggnog_run_index_sql) {
  # Launch mirai to handle the index creation
  eggnog_index_task <- mirai({
    worker_pg <- DBI::dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(), dbname = "glamr_data", host = "cayman.earth.lsa.umich.edu", port = "5432", user = "glamr_admin", password = "glamr2023")
    DBI::dbExecute(worker_pg, "SET maintenance_work_mem = '16GB'")
    for (sql in index_sql) DBI::dbExecute(worker_pg, sql)
    DBI::dbDisconnect(worker_pg)
    return("eggnog indices created successfully")
  }, index_sql = as.character(eggnog_index_sql))

  message("Indices for eggnog are being created in the background...")

  # To check if it's done later:
  unresolved(eggnog_index_task) # Returns TRUE if still running
  #eggnog_index_task[]          # Returns the result (blocks until finished)
} else {
  message("Index SQL (run with psql, then VACUUM (FREEZE, ANALYZE) both tables):")
  message(paste(eggnog_index_sql, collapse = ";\n"), ";")
}
```

```{r}
             marker = marker) %>% 
      select(sample, marker, clade, rpkm, mapped_reads) %>% 
      dbWriteTable(pg, "mc_clade_abunds", ., overwrite = FALSE, append = TRUE)
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("Error occurred while processing file:", path, "\n")
    cat("Error message:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
  })
}
```

## Amplicon ASVs (DADA2)

Loads the outputs of the amplicon pipeline (`data/projects/{dataset}/dada2.{target_spec}/`) for datasets with
`amplicon_pipeline_done`. `target_spec` is `{gene model}.{hmm start}-{hmm end}`, e.g. `16S_rRNA_bac.524-776`.

| Table | One row per | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `amplicon_primers` | primer | `pypelib/amplicon/primers.json`: sequence, direction, gene, HMM coordinates, and region |
| `amplicon_dada2_runs` | dataset × target_spec | gene, region, HMM coordinates, main primer pair, taxonomy DB, and load bookkeeping |
| `amplicon_sample_target` | sample × dataset | the gene, primers, and region the pipeline detected for each sample (`target_info.tsv`) |
| `amplicon_asv` | unique sequence | `asv_id` (MD5 of the sequence) and the sequence |
| `amplicon_asv_abundance` | ASV × sample × run | read counts (zeros dropped) |
| `amplicon_asv_taxonomy` | ASV × run × source × rank | taxonomy in long format, since rank names differ between SILVA, PR2, MIDORI2, and UNITE |

`asv_id` is the primary key: the MD5 hash of the ASV sequence, so the same sequence gets the same ID in every
dataset (the same scheme QIIME 2 uses). `local_asv_id` keeps the pipeline's own ID (`tasv1`, ...), which is only
unique within one DADA2 run. Abundance and taxonomy are linked to gene, region, and primers through
`dataset` + `target_spec` in `amplicon_dada2_runs`.

A run is loaded once, and deleted and reloaded when its DADA2 files are newer than the load
(`files_mtime` in `amplicon_dada2_runs`). The taxonomy DB recorded for a run is the one in `config/default.conf`
at load time.

```{r}
amplicon_config <- yaml::read_yaml("config/default.conf")

# Tables are created up front so asv_id can be the primary key and the column types are fixed
dbExecute(pg, "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS amplicon_asv (
                 asv_id text PRIMARY KEY, sequence text, length integer, gene text)")
dbExecute(pg, "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS amplicon_asv_abundance (
                 asv_id text, local_asv_id text, sample text, dataset text, target_spec text,
                 count integer, opposite_strand boolean)")
dbExecute(pg, "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS amplicon_asv_taxonomy (
                 asv_id text, local_asv_id text, dataset text, target_spec text, source text, db text,
                 rank_level smallint, rank text, taxon text)")
dbExecute(pg, "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS amplicon_sample_target (
                 sample text, dataset text, gene text, fwd_primer text, rev_primer text, region text,
                 fwd_hmmfrom integer, fwd_hmmto integer, rev_hmmfrom integer, rev_hmmto integer,
                 layout text, swapped text, overlap_pct text, override text, errors text)")
dbExecute(pg, "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS amplicon_dada2_runs (
                 dataset text, target_spec text, gene text, region text, hmm_start integer, hmm_end integer,
                 fwd_primer text, rev_primer text, n_samples integer, n_asvs integer,
                 taxonomy_db text, taxonomy_method text, files_mtime timestamptz, loaded_at timestamptz,
                 PRIMARY KEY (dataset, target_spec))")

# Primers: small reference table, rewritten every time so edits to primers.json carry through
amplicon_primers <- jsonlite::fromJSON("pypelib/amplicon/primers.json") %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  select(name, sequence, direction, gene_target, hmm_name, start, end, region, citation)

dbWriteTable(pg, "amplicon_primers", amplicon_primers, overwrite = TRUE)

# Region spanned by a primer pair, from the primers' region fields, e.g. "V4-" + "-V4" -> "V4", "V3-" + "-V4" -> "V3-V4"
primer_pair_region <- function(fwd_primer, rev_primer) {
  fwd_region <- str_remove(amplicon_primers$region[match(fwd_primer, amplicon_primers$name)], "-$")
  rev_region <- str_remove(amplicon_primers$region[match(rev_primer, amplicon_primers$name)], "^-")
  case_when(is.na(fwd_region) | is.na(rev_region) ~ NA_character_,
            fwd_region == rev_region ~ fwd_region,
            TRUE ~ str_c(fwd_region, "-", rev_region))
}

# DADA2 runs in finished datasets; the target_spec pattern skips leftovers such as *_OLD and *_ERROR
dada2_runs <- Sys.glob("data/projects/*/amplicon_pipeline_done") %>%
  dirname() %>%
  map(~ Sys.glob(file.path(.x, "dada2.*"))) %>%
  unlist() %>%
  data.frame(dir = .) %>%
  bind_cols(., unglue::unglue_data(.$dir, "data/projects/{dataset}/dada2.{target_spec}")) %>%
  filter(str_detect(target_spec, "^[A-Za-z0-9_]+\\.[0-9]+-[0-9]+$"),
         file.exists(file.path(dir, "asv_table.tsv"))) %>%
  mutate(gene = str_extract(target_spec, "^[^.]+"),
         hmm_start = as.integer(str_extract(target_spec, "(?<=\\.)[0-9]+")),
         hmm_end = as.integer(str_extract(target_spec, "[0-9]+$")),
         files_mtime = map(dir, ~ max(file.mtime(Sys.glob(file.path(.x, c("asv_table.tsv", "rep_seqs.fasta", "asvs.fasta", "taxonomy*.tsv"))))))) %>%
  unnest(files_mtime)

loaded_dada2_runs <- tbl(pg, "amplicon_dada2_runs") %>%
  select(dataset, target_spec, loaded_mtime = files_mtime) %>%
  collect()

# New runs, plus runs whose files changed since they were loaded (1 s slack for the timestamp round trip)
new_dada2_runs <- dada2_runs %>%
  left_join(loaded_dada2_runs, by = c("dataset", "target_spec")) %>%
  filter(is.na(loaded_mtime) | files_mtime > loaded_mtime + 1)

message(nrow(new_dada2_runs), " of ", nrow(dada2_runs), " DADA2 runs to load")

# Per-sample gene, primers, and region detected by the pipeline. Column sets differ between pipeline
# versions (e.g. model_rc vs swapped), so everything is read as character and only shared columns kept.
read_sample_targets <- function(dataset) {
  target_info <- read_tsv(file.path("data/projects", dataset, "target_info.tsv"),
                          col_types = cols(.default = "c"), show_col_types = FALSE)
  assignments_path <- file.path("data/projects", dataset, "amplicon_target_assignments.tsv")
  assignments <- if (file.exists(assignments_path)) {
    read_tsv(assignments_path, col_types = cols(.default = "c"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>% select(sample, override)
  } else tibble(sample = character(), override = character())

  target_info %>%
    select(any_of(c("sample", "model_name", "fwd_primer", "rev_primer", "fwd_hmmfrom", "fwd_hmmto",
                    "rev_hmmfrom", "rev_hmmto", "layout", "swapped", "overlap_pct", "errors"))) %>%
    left_join(assignments, by = "sample") %>%
    mutate(dataset = dataset,
           region = primer_pair_region(fwd_primer, rev_primer),
           across(any_of(c("fwd_hmmfrom", "fwd_hmmto", "rev_hmmfrom", "rev_hmmto")), as.integer)) %>%
    rename(gene = model_name) %>%
    relocate(sample, dataset, gene, fwd_primer, rev_primer, region)
}

# Taxonomy files are keyed by local ID (tasv1) in newer runs and by sequence in older ones
read_run_taxonomy <- function(path, asvs) {
  taxonomy <- read_tsv(path, col_types = cols(.default = "c"), show_col_types = FALSE)
  key <- if (all(str_detect(taxonomy$asv_id, "^tasv"))) "local_asv_id" else "sequence"

  taxonomy %>%
    rename(!!key := asv_id) %>%
    pivot_longer(-all_of(key), names_to = "rank", values_to = "taxon") %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(key))) %>%
    mutate(rank_level = row_number()) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    filter(!is.na(taxon)) %>%
    inner_join(asvs %>% select(asv_id, local_asv_id, sequence), by = key) %>%
    select(asv_id, local_asv_id, rank_level, rank, taxon)
}

load_dada2_run <- function(dir, dataset, target_spec, gene, hmm_start, hmm_end, files_mtime, sample_targets) {
  # asvs.fasta is rep_seqs.fasta after the HMM check, with opposite_strand flagged in the header
  fasta <- if (file.exists(file.path(dir, "asvs.fasta"))) file.path(dir, "asvs.fasta") else file.path(dir, "rep_seqs.fasta")
  seqs <- Biostrings::readDNAStringSet(fasta)
  asvs <- tibble(local_asv_id = str_extract(names(seqs), "^\\S+"),
                 opposite_strand = str_detect(names(seqs), "opposite_strand"),
                 sequence = toupper(as.character(seqs))) %>%
    mutate(asv_id = as.character(openssl::md5(sequence)),
           length = nchar(sequence)) %>%
    relocate(asv_id)

  abundance <- read_tsv(file.path(dir, "asv_table.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    pivot_longer(-sample, names_to = "local_asv_id", values_to = "count") %>%
    filter(count > 0) %>%
    inner_join(asvs %>% select(asv_id, local_asv_id, opposite_strand), by = "local_asv_id") %>%
    mutate(dataset = dataset, target_spec = target_spec, count = as.integer(count)) %>%
    select(asv_id, local_asv_id, sample, dataset, target_spec, count, opposite_strand)

  # Main taxonomy plus the PR2 organelle reclassification for 16S_rRNA_bac chloroplast and mitochondria ASVs
  taxonomy_sources <- tibble(source = c("main", names(amplicon_config$amplicon_organelle_taxonomy))) %>%
    mutate(path = file.path(dir, if_else(source == "main", "taxonomy.tsv", str_c("taxonomy_", source, ".tsv"))),
           db = if_else(source == "main",
                        basename(amplicon_config$amplicon_taxonomy_dbs[[gene]] %||% NA_character_),
                        map_chr(source, ~ basename(amplicon_config$amplicon_organelle_taxonomy[[.x]]$db %||% NA_character_)))) %>%
    filter(file.exists(path))

  taxonomy <- taxonomy_sources %>%
    mutate(tax = map(path, read_run_taxonomy, asvs = asvs)) %>%
    select(source, db, tax) %>%
    unnest(tax) %>%
    mutate(dataset = dataset, target_spec = target_spec, rank_level = as.integer(rank_level)) %>%
    select(asv_id, local_asv_id, dataset, target_spec, source, db, rank_level, rank, taxon)

  # Main primer pair for the run, from the samples in its ASV table
  run_primers <- sample_targets %>%
    filter(sample %in% abundance$sample) %>%
    count(fwd_primer, rev_primer, sort = TRUE) %>%
    slice_head(n = 1)

  run <- tibble(dataset = dataset, target_spec = target_spec, gene = gene,
                region = primer_pair_region(run_primers$fwd_primer[1], run_primers$rev_primer[1]),
                hmm_start = hmm_start, hmm_end = hmm_end,
                fwd_primer = run_primers$fwd_primer[1], rev_primer = run_primers$rev_primer[1],
                n_samples = n_distinct(abundance$sample), n_asvs = nrow(asvs),
                taxonomy_db = taxonomy_sources$db[taxonomy_sources$source == "main"][1],
                taxonomy_method = if_else(gene %in% names(amplicon_config$amplicon_taxonomy_vsearch), "vsearch consensus", "assignTaxonomy"),
                files_mtime = files_mtime, loaded_at = Sys.time())

  # One transaction per run, so a failure doesn't leave it half loaded
  dbWithTransaction(pg, {
    for (table in c("amplicon_asv_abundance", "amplicon_asv_taxonomy", "amplicon_dada2_runs")) {
      dbExecute(pg, str_glue("DELETE FROM {table} WHERE dataset = $1 AND target_spec = $2"), params = list(dataset, target_spec))
    }

    existing_asvs <- tbl(pg, "amplicon_asv") %>% filter(asv_id %in% local(asvs$asv_id)) %>% pull(asv_id)
    asvs %>%
      filter(!asv_id %in% existing_asvs) %>%
      distinct(asv_id, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
      transmute(asv_id, sequence, length, gene = gene) %>%
      dbWriteTable(pg, "amplicon_asv", ., append = TRUE)

    dbWriteTable(pg, "amplicon_asv_abundance", abundance, append = TRUE)
    dbWriteTable(pg, "amplicon_asv_taxonomy", taxonomy, append = TRUE)
    dbWriteTable(pg, "amplicon_dada2_runs", run, append = TRUE)
  })

  message(dataset, " ", target_spec, ": ", nrow(asvs), " ASVs, ", nrow(abundance), " abundance rows, ", nrow(taxonomy), " taxonomy rows")
}

# Sample targets are replaced for every dataset with a run being (re)loaded
amplicon_sample_targets <- new_dada2_runs %>%
  distinct(dataset) %>%
  filter(file.exists(file.path("data/projects", dataset, "target_info.tsv"))) %>%
  pull(dataset) %>%
  map(read_sample_targets) %>%
  list_rbind()

if (nrow(amplicon_sample_targets) > 0) {
  dbWithTransaction(pg, {
    dbExecute(pg, "DELETE FROM amplicon_sample_target WHERE dataset = ANY($1)",
              params = list(str_c("{", str_c(unique(amplicon_sample_targets$dataset), collapse = ","), "}")))
    dbWriteTable(pg, "amplicon_sample_target", amplicon_sample_targets, append = TRUE)
  })
}

pwalk(new_dada2_runs %>% select(dir, dataset, target_spec, gene, hmm_start, hmm_end, files_mtime),
      load_dada2_run,
      sample_targets = amplicon_sample_targets,
      .progress = TRUE)

# Indexes (IF NOT EXISTS, so re-running the chunk is safe)
dbExecute(pg, 'CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "amplicon_asv_abundance_asv_id" ON "amplicon_asv_abundance" ("asv_id")')
dbExecute(pg, 'CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "amplicon_asv_abundance_sample" ON "amplicon_asv_abundance" ("sample")')
dbExecute(pg, 'CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "amplicon_asv_abundance_run" ON "amplicon_asv_abundance" ("dataset", "target_spec")')
dbExecute(pg, 'CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "amplicon_asv_taxonomy_asv_id" ON "amplicon_asv_taxonomy" ("asv_id")')
dbExecute(pg, 'CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "amplicon_asv_taxonomy_run" ON "amplicon_asv_taxonomy" ("dataset", "target_spec")')
dbExecute(pg, 'CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "amplicon_asv_taxonomy_taxon" ON "amplicon_asv_taxonomy" ("rank", "taxon")')
dbExecute(pg, 'CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "amplicon_sample_target_sample" ON "amplicon_sample_target" ("sample")')
```

```{r}
    # #                        abund_w_subtax = "numeric",
    # #                        abund_direct = "numeric",
    # #                        sample = "text"
    # #                        )
    # 
    # benchmark %>%
    #       relocate(sample,rule) %>%
    #       dbWriteTable(pg, "benchmarks", ., overwrite = FALSE)

# Function for reading the summary tsv and saving it to the database
read_benchmarks_to_pg <- function(path, sample, rule) {
  print(sample)
  tryCatch({
    read_tsv(path,show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
      janitor::clean_names() %>% 
      mutate(sample = sample, 
             rule = rule, 
             h_m_s = as.character(h_m_s),
             mod_time = fs::file_info(path) %>% 
               pull(modification_time)) %>% 
      dplyr::relocate(sample,rule) %>% 
      dbWriteTable(pg, "benchmarks", ., overwrite = FALSE, append = TRUE)
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("Error occurred while processing file:", path, "\n")
    cat("Error message:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
  })
}

# Load new summaries into the database
# Drop existing indices [speeds up loading of new data]
sql('DROP INDEX public.benchmarks_sample') %>% DBI::dbSendQuery(pg, .)
sql('DROP INDEX public.benchmarks_rule') %>% DBI::dbSendQuery(pg, .)

pg <- DBI::dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(),dbname = "glamr_data", host = "cayman.earth.lsa.umich.edu", port = "5432", user = "glamr_admin", password = "glamr2023")
# Append new data
purrr::pwalk(.l = list(new_benchmark_tsvs$path,
                  new_benchmark_tsvs$sample,
                  new_benchmark_tsvs$rule),
             .f = read_benchmarks_to_pg,.progress = TRUE)

# Recreate indices
sql('CREATE INDEX "benchmarks_sample" ON "benchmarks" ("sample")') %>% DBI::dbSendQuery(pg, .)
sql('CREATE INDEX "benchmarks_rule" ON "benchmarks" ("rule")') %>% DBI::dbSendQuery(pg, .)
```

#### Antismash assembly
##### Counts
```{r}
antismash_assembly_pg <- tbl(pg, "antismash_assembly_counts")

antismash_assembly_samples <- get_pg_table_samples(pg, "antismash_assembly_counts", "sample")

antismash_assembly_files <- Sys.glob("data/omics/metagenomes/*/antismash8_assembly/summaries/counts.tsv") %>% 
  data.frame(path = .) %>% 
  unglue::unglue_unnest(path, "data/omics/{sample_type}/{sample}/antismash8_assembly/summaries/counts.tsv",remove = FALSE)

new_antismash_assembly_files <- antismash_assembly_files %>% 
  filter(!sample %in% antismash_assembly_samples$sample,
         str_detect(sample, "^samp_*") | str_detect(sample, "^coassembly_") | str_detect(sample, "^GVHDsamp_")) %>% 
  mutate(fs::file_info(path))

#path = new_antismash_assembly_files$path[1]
#sample_name = new_antismash_assembly_files$sample[1]
read_antismash_counts <- function(path, sample_name){
  
  counts_df <- read_tsv(path,comment = "#") %>% 
    mutate(sample = sample_name) %>% 
    pivot_longer(-c(sample, record, total_count, description), names_to = "group", values_to = "count") %>% 
    select(sample,group, count)
  
  
  # # Only used when creating the table for the first time, for all subsequent additions,
  # # append = TRUE should be added as the field types are already established
  # postgres_col_types = c(sample = 'text',
  #                        group = "text",
  #                        count = 'integer')
  # 
  # #First run to create table
  # dbWriteTable(pg,"antismash_assembly_counts",counts_df,overwrite = FALSE, field.types = postgres_col_types)

  dbWriteTable(pg,"antismash_assembly_counts",counts_df,overwrite = FALSE, append = TRUE)
  
  return(NULL)
}

# For the indexes created by this script
sql('DROP INDEX public.antismash_assembly_counts_sample') %>% DBI::dbSendQuery(pg, .)
sql('DROP INDEX public.antismash_assembly_counts_group') %>% DBI::dbSendQuery(pg, .)

walk2(new_antismash_assembly_files$path, new_antismash_assembly_files$sample, read_antismash_counts,.progress = TRUE)

sql('CREATE INDEX "antismash_assembly_counts_sample" ON "antismash_assembly_counts" ("sample")') %>% DBI::dbSendQuery(pg, .)
sql('CREATE INDEX "antismash_assembly_counts_group" ON "antismash_assembly_counts" ("group")') %>%  DBI::dbSendQuery(pg, .)
```

## EukCC
```{r}
# Get DREP results that are already loaded into the database
existing_eukcc_annotations <- tbl(pg, "eukcc") %>% 
  select(sample) %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  collect() 

# Find all DREP results
eukcc_paths <- Sys.glob("data/omics/metagenomes/*/bins/eukcc/eukcc.csv") %>% 
  data.frame(path = .) %>% 
  bind_cols(.,unglue::unglue_data(.$path,"data/omics/{sample_type}/{sample}/bins/eukcc/eukcc.csv")) %>% 
  bind_cols(file.info(.$path))

# Filter list of summary tsvs to only those not already loaded into the database
new_eukcc <- eukcc_paths %>% 
  filter(
      !sample %in% existing_eukcc_annotations$sample,
      (str_detect(sample, "^samp_") | str_detect(sample, "^coassembly_") | str_detect(sample, "^GVHDsamp_")))

# Initialize the mirai cluster for parallel csv parsing prior to upload
# Use parallel::detectCores() - 1 to leave a core for the OS
library(mirai)
n_cores <- parallel::detectCores() - 1
daemons(n_cores)

# Execute in Parallel
message(paste("Processing", nrow(new_eukcc), "samples across", n_cores, "cores..."))

everywhere({
  library(dplyr)
  library(readr)
  library(stringr)
  library(fs)
})

read_eukcc_parallel <- function(path, sample) {
  tryCatch({
    # Explicit column types: header-only files (no bins passing EukCC) otherwise
    # get guessed as all-character and can't be combined with the others
    df <- readr::read_tsv(path, show_col_types = FALSE,
                          col_types = readr::cols(bin = "c", completeness = "d", contamination = "d", ncbi_lng = "c")) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        bin = stringr::str_remove(bin, "\\.fa$"),
        sample = sample,
        ncbi_tax = as.numeric(stringr::str_remove(ncbi_lng, ".*-")) # bigint in postgres
      ) %>%
      #separate_wider_delim(cols = ncbi_lng,delim = "-",names_sep = "_",too_few = "align_start")
      dplyr::rename(ncbi_lineage = "ncbi_lng") %>%
      dplyr::relocate(sample)

    return(df)
  }, error = function(e) return(conditionMessage(e)))
}

combined_eukcc_results <- mirai_map(
  .x = new_eukcc %>% select(path,sample),
  .f = read_eukcc_parallel
)

# This waits for all workers to finish and binds the resulting data frames
eukcc_results_list <- combined_eukcc_results[]

# read_eukcc_parallel returns the error message instead of a data frame when a file fails to parse
failed_eukcc <- eukcc_results_list %>% discard(is.data.frame)
if (length(failed_eukcc) > 0) {
  warning(length(failed_eukcc), " EukCC files failed to parse and were skipped:\n",
          paste(new_eukcc$path[!map_lgl(eukcc_results_list, is.data.frame)], unlist(failed_eukcc), sep = ": ", collapse = "\n"))
}

combined_eukcc_data <- eukcc_results_list %>%
  keep(is.data.frame) %>%
  list_rbind()

# Shut down daemons once data is collected
daemons(0)

# Database Upload
if (nrow(combined_eukcc_data) > 0) {
  message("Uploading to Postgres...")
  
  # Clean up indices before bulk load
  dbExecute(pg, 'DROP INDEX IF EXISTS public.eukcc_bin')
  dbExecute(pg, 'DROP INDEX IF EXISTS public.eukcc_sample')
  dbExecute(pg, 'DROP INDEX IF EXISTS public.eukcc_tax')

  dbWriteTable(pg, "eukcc", combined_eukcc_data, append = TRUE, row.names = FALSE)

  # Recreate indices
  dbExecute(pg, 'CREATE INDEX "eukcc_bin" ON "eukcc" ("bin")')
  dbExecute(pg, 'CREATE INDEX "eukcc_sample" ON "eukcc" ("sample")')
  dbExecute(pg, 'CREATE INDEX "eukcc_tax" ON "eukcc" ("ncbi_tax")')
  
  message("Success!")
}
```
